facts.raw_span: a 2-year history of an enlarging, intermittently painful, purplish lump in her left ear canal
cracking and pus-filled sores at the site
a 3.5 × 2.5 cm purplish-red mass in the left external ear canal
irregular, friable surface and bleeding on minimal contact
Contrast-enhanced CT of the mastoids showed a lobulated mass in the cutis and subcutis of the left auricle
extending into the external acoustic canal and into the left parotid space
bilateral level II–IV cervical lymph nodes up to 0.6 cm in diameter
CT angiography demonstrated marked vascularity of the mass
supplied by branches of the left superficial temporal and posterior auricular arteries
Incisional biopsy revealed atypical cells and granulomatous inflammation
a provisional diagnosis of an auricular malignant tumor without a clear histopathological subtype

concepts.why: The presence of a rapidly growing, painful, and bleeding mass in the ear canal, along with atypical cells and granulomatous inflammation on biopsy, suggests a malignant tumor such as Rhabdomyosarcoma.

The combination of a long-standing, intermittently painful mass in the ear canal, with cracking and pus-filled sores, and granulomatous inflammation on biopsy, is consistent with Langerhans Cell Histiocytosis.

The presence of a rapidly growing, painful, and bleeding mass in the ear canal, with marked vascularity on CT angiography, and a provisional diagnosis of a malignant tumor, suggests Merkel Cell Carcinoma as a possible diagnosis.

The presence of a rapidly growing, painful, and bleeding mass in the ear canal, with a lobulated appearance on CT, and a provisional diagnosis of a malignant tumor, suggests Squamous Cell Carcinoma as a possible diagnosis.

The presence of a slowly growing, painful mass in the ear canal, with a lobulated appearance on CT, and a provisional diagnosis of a malignant tumor, suggests Basal Cell Carcinoma as a possible diagnosis.

The presence of a rapidly growing, painful, and bleeding mass in the ear canal, with marked vascularity on CT angiography, and a provisional diagnosis of a malignant tumor, suggests Angiosarcoma as a possible diagnosis.
The combination of a long-standing, intermittently painful mass in the ear canal, with cracking and pus-filled sores, and atypical cells on biopsy, is consistent with Ewing Sarcoma.

The presence of a rapidly growing, painful, and bleeding mass in the ear canal, with a lobulated appearance on CT, and a provisional diagnosis of a malignant tumor, suggests Osteosarcoma as a possible diagnosis.
The presence of a slowly growing, painful mass in the ear canal, with a lobulated appearance on CT, and a provisional diagnosis of a malignant tumor, suggests Chondrosarcoma as a possible diagnosis.

The presence of a rapidly growing, painful, and bleeding mass in the ear canal, with marked vascularity on CT angiography, and a provisional diagnosis of a malignant tumor, suggests Leiomyosarcoma as a possible diagnosis.

rationales.F01: The patient's 2-year history of an enlarging, intermittently painful, purplish lump in her left ear canal suggests a possible malignant tumor, which is more typical of Rhabdomyosarcoma.
rationales.F08: The marked vascularity of the mass, as demonstrated by CT angiography, is more characteristic of Angiosarcoma.
rationales.F10: The presence of atypical cells and granulomatous inflammation in the incisional biopsy is highly suggestive of a malignant tumor, with Rhabdomyosarcoma and Angiosarcoma being more likely.
rationales.F11: The provisional diagnosis of an auricular malignant tumor without a clear histopathological subtype, combined with the patient's symptoms and biopsy results, strongly suggests Rhabdomyosarcoma or Angiosarcoma.
